### Step 1 — Scene
A meal of egg fried rice and stir-fried noodles with vegetables and some apparent meat pieces. Both plates appear to belong to the meal. There is also water and a wrapped cone-shaped item; the wrapped contents are not visible, so I exclude them.

### Step 2 — Vessels
Two shallow disposable plates, each approximately **23 cm diameter**.

Area of each: 3.14 × 11.5² ≈ **415 cm²**.

### Steps 3–6 — Items, coverage, volume and weight
Areas below are non-overlapping estimates. Oil and sauce coating the food are included in the relevant food weights and energy densities.

| Plate / item | Plate area covered | Area | Average height | Gross volume | Bulk density | Weight |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| Fried rice: rice with oil/seasoning | 42% | 174 cm² | 1.7 cm | 296 ml | 0.8 | 237 g |
| Fried rice: egg | 3% | 12 cm² | 0.8 cm | 10 ml | 0.95 | 9 g |
| Fried rice: peas, carrot and other vegetables | 3% | 12 cm² | 0.8 cm | 10 ml | 0.6 | 6 g |
| Noodles with sauce/oil | 34% | 141 cm² | 1.65 cm | 233 ml | 0.8 | 186 g |
| Noodle vegetables: cabbage, carrot and onion | 8% | 33 cm² | 1.1 cm | 36 ml | 0.6 | 22 g |
| Apparent meat pieces in noodles | 5% | 21 cm² | 1.1 cm | 23 ml | 0.95 | 22 g |

Coverage check: **48% of the rice plate** and **47% of the noodle plate**. Both have substantial empty rims, consistent with these estimates.

### Step 7 — Energy
Using cooked, as-plated energy densities:

- Rice with absorbed oil/seasoning: 237 g × 175 kcal/100 g = **415 kcal**
- Egg: 9 g × 160 = **14 kcal**
- Rice vegetables: 6 g × 60 = **4 kcal**
- Sauced noodles: 186 g × 180 = **335 kcal**
- Stir-fried vegetables: 22 g × 70 = **15 kcal**
- Meat pieces: 22 g × 200 = **44 kcal**

### Step 8 — Sanity check
Total estimated edible food: **482 g**, providing approximately **827 kcal**. Roughly 250 g on each partly filled plate is plausible. The main uncertainties are pile height, oil content and the identity of the small meat pieces.
